target_customer: Medical practices that release patient records, and the patients and insurers who request them
problem: Most medical records were still moved by fax and courier, so releasing records to patients and other providers was slow.
business_model: Software installed at practices to automate records release; later a subscription HIPAA texting platform
product_category: Healthcare records exchange, later secure messaging

founders.name: Michael Wasser
founders.background_notes: YC bio calls him a hacker focused on social impact building open source projects.

founders.name: Heather Milone
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. No background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with many EHR systems and meeting HIPAA requirements were the hard parts for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Installed software at practices gives some stickiness, but records release was a thin wedge and the company later changed focus.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying was found. The company changed product focus instead.

market_need_then: Faxes and couriers still moved most medical records; the 2017 raise coverage described records release as broken.

branding.domain_note: Product site is bloomtext.com rather than bloomapi.com.

rebrands.to: BloomText (secure texting product), same legal entity BloomAPI Inc.
rebrands.why: Not stated; a GitHub README says BloomAPI is now a company with a different focus.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand and the API name no longer matches the texting product.

outcome_analysis: BloomAPI raised a 2.4M seed in 2017 for records release, then appears to have shifted to BloomText, a HIPAA texting product still selling in 2026. The company survived on a small team, but no growth round, acquisition or traction figures were found.
notes: The pivot to texting is supported by the live bloomtext.com site and a directory, but no dated pivot source was found, so the pivots list is empty. CB Insights labels the July 2017 round Series A and lists a total of 2.77M over three rounds; this is an aggregator and not recorded. The Geekwire article could not be fetched. Competitors are empty because no source dated near the batch was found; later directories name Particle Health, Redox and Human API. Founder education and prior employers not found.
